source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.source_content: For an analytic double fibration with incidence cotangent relation $C_Z\subset(T^*G\setminus0)\times(T^*X\setminus0)$, let $\pi_L:C_Z\longrightarrow T^*G\setminus0$, $\pi_L(g,\eta;x,\xi)=(g,\eta)$. The double fibration satisfies the global Bolker condition if $\pi_L$ is an injective immersion. The pointwise clause is a singleton fiber and injective differential.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.rationale: A small schematic could orient the left/data and right/object cotangent factors and distinguish the global injective-immersion condition from the pointwise fiber-plus-rank condition. The definition is already complete in text, so this is an editorial aid.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.draw_or_check: Show $C_Z$ with projections $\pi_L:C_Z\to T^*G\setminus0$ and $\pi_R:C_Z\to T^*X\setminus0$; label a data covector $(g,\eta)$, its full fiber $\pi_L^{-1}(g,\eta)$, the unique point $c=(g,\eta;x,\xi)$ in the pointwise case, and the injective differential $d\pi_L|_c$. Do not imply that pointwise fiber uniqueness alone gives the global condition.

source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.kind: finite-dimensional linear map and kernel schematic
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.source_content: There are $m=rs$ sampled direction pairs and $N=m+1$ partition slabs; $F\in\mathbb C^{m\times N}$ maps slab coefficients $c$ to sampled Born data, and a nonzero $c\in\ker F$ gives a nonzero piecewise-constant contrast with all samples zero.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.rationale: The dimension-count mechanism is a concrete linear algebra map embedded in a finite-sample inverse problem; a compact schematic can connect the sample rows, slab coefficients, and indistinguishable nonzero contrast. Text already proves the claim, so this is editorial.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.draw_or_check: Draw $\mathbb C^{m+1}$ (slab coefficients $c_1,\ldots,c_{m+1}$ for $E_1,\ldots,E_{m+1}$) under $F$ to $\mathbb C^m$ (rows indexed by $(\theta_b,d_a)$, $\xi_{ba}=k(\theta_b-d_a)/(2\pi)$); mark a nonzero $c\in\ker F$ and the contrast $h=\sum_nc_n1_{E_n}\ne0$ with $\mathcal B_kh(\theta_b,d_a)=0$. State that this is the finite first-Born map, not exact nonlinear data.

existing_diagrams_reviewed.result: The two measured antipodal arcs and missing vertical covector match the source description.
The vectors $kd$, $k\theta$, and chord $k(\theta-d)$ match the source explanation.
The displayed square labels the finite coefficient map, partial reconstruction, coefficient sum, and $L^2(\mathbb P)$ class consistently with the surrounding definitions.

diagram_review.reason: Two optional diagram candidates are directly supported by explicit maps and relations in the source text. Existing TikZ diagrams were checked against their source mathematics; no confirmed diagram errors were observed.
